# Kyoto 5-Day Spring Trip Plan

A relaxed, temple-and-garden-focused Kyoto plan for **2 adults** with a **mid-range station-area hotel** and a **total on-the-ground budget of JPY 180,000**.
This version keeps daily movement efficient, uses short transit hops, and stays within a realistic sightseeing pace for April 10–14, 2026.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan

| Day | Focus | Main Stops | Transit Tip | Est. Cost for 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apr 10 | Higashiyama arrival day | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Yasaka Shrine, Gion evening walk | Use bus + short walks; taxi back if tired | JPY 19,000 |
| Apr 11 | Arashiyama gardens and river | Tenryu-ji, Bamboo Grove, Okochi Sanso, Togetsukyo Bridge | JR or Hankyu to Arashiyama; keep walking light | JPY 24,000 |
| Apr 12 | Central Kyoto temples | Nijo Castle, Kyoto Gyoen, Nishiki Market, Pontocho dinner | Subway + taxi for the slowest leg | JPY 22,000 |
| Apr 13 | Northern temple day | Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, Ninna-ji, optional Daitoku-ji area | Bus works, but taxi saves time and energy | JPY 25,000 |
| Apr 14 | Eastern Kyoto finale | Nanzen-ji, Eikan-do, Philosopher’s Path, souvenir lunch | Subway to Keage, then walk the corridor | JPY 18,000 |

## Kyoto Itinerary by Day

### Day 1: Higashiyama Arrival and Easy Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, and keep the first half-day light. If you land early, visit **Kiyomizu-dera** and nearby lanes.
- **Afternoon:** Walk **Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka**, then continue to **Yasaka Shrine** and the Maruyama Park area.
Media: Alt=Afternoon:** Walk **Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka**, then continue to **Yasaka Shrine** and the Maruyama Park area, Kyoto, Japan
- **Food:** Try **yudofu**, **matcha sweets**, or a simple **kaiseki lunch** if arrival timing allows.
- **Pace:** Moderate; this is a good day to avoid packing in too much.
- **Estimated cost:** Temple entries, local transit, snacks, and dinner: **JPY 19,000**.

### Day 2: Arashiyama Gardens and Riverside Views
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Start early at **Tenryu-ji Garden** and the **Bamboo Grove** before crowds build.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Okochi Sanso Garden** if you want a quieter, scenic stop; finish at **Togetsukyo Bridge**.
- **Food:** Lunch on **tofu cuisine**, **soba**, or a riverside set meal.
- **Pace:** Light to moderate; this area is best enjoyed slowly.
- **Estimated cost:** Transit, garden entries, lunch, and dinner: **JPY 24,000**.

### Day 3: Central Kyoto Temples and Market Food
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Nijo Castle** first, then head to **Kyoto Gyoen** for a calmer garden walk.
- **Afternoon:** Explore **Nishiki Market** for local food sampling; keep portions small so you can taste more.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Afternoon:** Explore **Nishiki Market** for local food sampling; keep portions small so you can taste more, Kyoto, Japan
- **Evening:** Have dinner in **Pontocho** or nearby downtown Kyoto.
- **Food:** Look for **dashimaki**, **pickles**, **yuba**, and seasonal sweets.
- **Pace:** Moderate; mostly flat walking with easy transit.
- **Estimated cost:** Admissions, market food, transit, and dinner: **JPY 22,000**.

### Day 4: Northern Kyoto Temple Circuit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Go early to **Kinkaku-ji** to avoid the busiest period.
- **Afternoon:** Continue to **Ryoan-ji** and **Ninna-ji**; if energy is good, add a short detour to the **Daitoku-ji** area.
- **Food:** A simple **udon** or **tempura set** works well between temple visits.
- **Pace:** Moderate to slightly brisk because this area is spread out.
- **Estimated cost:** Transit, temple fees, lunch, and dinner: **JPY 25,000**.

### Day 5: Philosopher’s Path and Eastern Kyoto Farewell
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Morning:** Start at **Nanzen-ji**, then continue to **Eikan-do** for garden views and temple atmosphere.
- **Afternoon:** Walk part of the **Philosopher’s Path** at an easy pace; finish with a final café or souvenir stop.
- **Food:** Have a farewell lunch with **obanzai** or a seasonal Kyoto lunch set.
- **Pace:** Relaxed; this is the best day for a slower final stroll.
- **Estimated cost:** Transit, temple entries, lunch, and snacks: **JPY 18,000**.

## Budget Fit and Hotel Strategy

- **Hotel target:** Mid-range hotel near **Kyoto Station**, **Gojo Station**, or **Shijo/Karasuma** area.
- **Suggested lodging budget:** **JPY 14,000–20,000 per night per room**.
- **5-night total lodging estimate:** **JPY 70,000–100,000**.
- **Remaining daily budget for both adults:** roughly **JPY 16,000–22,000 per day** after hotel, which is workable for temples, transit, meals, and a few paid gardens.

### Realistic total spend
- **Hotel:** JPY 80,000–95,000
- **Sightseeing admissions:** JPY 8,000–15,000
- **Local transport:** JPY 10,000–16,000
- **Food and drinks:** JPY 50,000–65,000
- **Buffer/souvenirs:** JPY 8,000–15,000

**Expected total:** about **JPY 156,000–191,000**
To stay safely under **JPY 180,000**, aim for:
- one hotel room near Kyoto Station in the **JPY 15,000–18,000/night** range,
- mostly subway/JR plus occasional taxi,
- one nicer dinner, not every night,
- modest paid garden add-ons.

## Transit Tips for a Comfortable Pace

- **Best base area:** **Kyoto Station** is the most practical for arrivals, departures, and easy rail access.
- **Best backup base:** **Gojo** or **Karasuma** if you want a slightly calmer neighborhood with good subway access.
- **Use taxis strategically:** especially after long temple days or when bus transfers would eat time.
- **Walking limit:** this plan keeps most sight-to-sight walks to **20 minutes or less**.
- **Start early:** temples are much more enjoyable before mid-morning crowds.
- **Keep one flexible slot daily:** Kyoto is best when you leave room for a café break or an extra temple garden.
